races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ballybunion
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type stepping up from 6f to 7f, a trip yet to be won over; trainer Michael Bell has only one winner from 18 in the past 14 days and the 84-day absence adds an element of uncertainty, though the horse has placed twice on good ground and conditions here are straightforward.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts but has back-to-back seconds two and three starts back to his name, and he has run over today's trip; the concern is a lengthy 84-day absence and an unplaced effort last time out suggest he may need this to find his best.

runners_data.name: Generous Rascal
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted and in fair recent form (three runs placing in last six), but this horse's true hold-up style means it is operating away from the rear where it naturally wants to be; Dylan Cunha's yard is running at a solid 11% and the 13-day turnaround suggests freshness, though competing from a compromised tactical position in a bunched finish.|
runners_data.comment: Generous Rascal shaped with promise when third three starts back and arrives here fit on a 13-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; yet to win in recent starts, but our rating of 83 marks him out as the one to beat from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Lessay
runners_data.note: Has won over course and distance (1/7f/STA) and places repeatedly at AW on standard going — the most relevant course-and-distance profile in this field; wears a hood and, though genuinely a hold-up type, its excellent AW record suggests it can adapt; the 33-day break looks fine for a five-year-old of this profile.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our figures and up against it on an official mark of 61, Lessay does at least bring recent winning form and distance-and-going experience to the table, but a patchy overall record in recent starts and stall 11 make him hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Angels' Share
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (five runs without a place outside one fifth), and although this three-year-old is a natural closer, it has struggled repeatedly at 7f on good and soft; the structural redistribution away from the rear compounds what is already a worrying form line, and Cieren Fallon's booking does not override the lack of evidence for a win here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Angels' Share does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 23 days off suggests she's fresh; however, she's been struggling for form lately, and carrying 131 lb from stall 10 makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Al Muqdad
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on this consistent six-year-old who has placed in 11 of 15 runs on similar going — outstanding going suitability; wore a visor and ran only eight days ago, and while form shows a sequence of minor placings, the class question is whether he can convert one at OR 70.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and lightly race-fit after just eight days, Al Muqdad boasts experience over today's trip and going, and his three minor placings — third last time out, and a second three starts back — underpin a rating of 75; the main concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Gunfighter
runners_data.note: Won last time out over course and distance (1/7f/STA) and has five runs placing from 15 on this surface — a key positive; Jack Gilligan continues the partnership and the 26-day gap is ideal; his pattern of getting the job done on AW 7f in compressed finishes makes him one of the most relevant profiles in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Gunfighter arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving him every reason to go well here; the concern is that his record in recent starts shows that win surrounded by some patchy efforts.

runners_data.name: Kit Gabriel
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with solid AW 7f placing profile (three times placed from 12 at STA), Tyler Heard takes a lesser-profile booking; trainer Simon Pearce has just one runner in the 14-day window; has won on this surface and consistently places at this course and distance, making him a durable if not explosive contender.|
runners_data.comment: Kit Gabriel shaped well when second three starts back and third four starts back, and he returns in good order on 24 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the main concern is that he has been winless in recent starts and must shoulder 140 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Merry
runners_data.note: Style is unknown — has only three runs, all on AW standard going, showing 3-4-5 form; a 92-day absence makes the form difficult to project and there is limited evidence of a tactical identity; for Daniel Muscutt, this is a speculative ride, but the horse has improved with each run and a sprint finish may suit an unexposed type.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and 92 days off the track are the obvious concerns, but she has run over today's trip and going before and that placed effort three starts back at least shows ability; 135 lb from stall one is the neutral backdrop.

runners_data.name: Quick Quasar
runners_data.note: Won last time at 7f AW 32 days ago with a promising turn of foot, wears blinkers and is a hold-up type that has been pushed into midfield on the map; Luke Morris is an experienced AW pilot and if Quick Quasar can find a forward enough position from the redistribution, recent winning form makes it dangerous in a sprint finish.|
runners_data.comment: Quick Quasar has finished seventh and ninth in his last two starts, and his speed rating of 56 leaves him well below the principals on these figures; ranked tenth of twelve, he's hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Espanita
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has one AW win from seven runs on standard going, but has failed to place in last two at 8f and 9f; dropping back to 7f is a positive and Charlie Johnston's yard has three winners from 45 in the past fortnight; the redistribution away from natural rear position adds tactical friction to a horse already searching for form.|
runners_data.comment: Espanita has finished sixth, ninth and eighth in her last three starts, making her hard to fancy despite a win six starts back. She has experience of today's trip and going, but ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, the case for her is thin.

runners_data.name: Piazza
runners_data.note: Has never won on standard going (0W0P from six AW runs) and despite minor placing form on good ground, this is a significant weakness in this specific context; Sean Bowen takes the ride but the going suitability stat is stark, and being a hold-up type placed into midfield does not help a horse with fragile confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third on two occasions in recent starts yet winless in her last five, Piazza has experience over today's trip and arrives here fit on a 15-day break, with her trainer firing at 26% recently; the weight of 128 lb from stall 12 may test her.

runners_data.name: Uniter
runners_data.note: Has been absent 88 days and the form string includes a pulled-up run (P), with no win or place recorded from eight AW runs; George Bass is an inexperienced claimer and Denis Coakley's yard has had no winners from six in the past two weeks — combination of fitness doubt, weak form and tactical displacement makes this one of the weakest profiles in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Uniter is hard to fancy as the bottom-ranked runner on our figures; 88 days off adds another query, though he has run over today's trip and going before, and stall two is his.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field, the race is set to begin with a tentative early gallop as the field — composed almost entirely of hold-up types — waits for others to commit, before inevitably collapsing into a compressed, sprint-finish dynamic from the two-furlong pole. Gunfighter and Kit Gabriel carry the strongest AW form at this venue and distance and are likely to sit in the early-to-mid portion of the pack as the pace drifts along at a moderate tempo. The absence of any genuine leader means the race will be decided by who can find clear air earliest in the straight, benefiting horses with a turn of foot rather than those who need a true-run gallop to sustain a long run. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can all settle at the back — Generous Rascal, Quick Quasar, Angels' Share, Lessay, Espanita, Piazza and Uniter are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield because the map cannot place them all at the rear; of these, Lessay (has won here over 7f) and Quick Quasar (sharp recent win at 7f AW) are best placed to actually secure a forward enough berth to matter. This race shape — slow early, sprint finish — most favours horses who can race handy enough to avoid traffic and explode late over the final two furlongs, meaning genuine hold-up horses with a reliable finishing kick hold the structural edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace drifts as expected and the field bunches turning for home, triggering a mass sprint in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Horses positioned handy enough to avoid traffic will be first to pounce, with the short straight at Wolverhampton offering little time to make up ground from the rear; Gunfighter and Kit Gabriel, proven at this venue and distance on AW, are well-suited to this compressed finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one horse — likely Lessay or Quick Quasar — secures a handy midfield berth and kicks first into the straight before rivals can respond.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop allows an enterprising ride to coast into a challenging position from the two-furlong mark, with the Wolverhampton 7f configuration rewarding those who commit early; Lessay's strong AW course-and-distance record (1/7f/STA win) and Quick Quasar's recent 7f AW victory make them the most credible beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the sprint develops with enough separation through the field that a true closer can thread through and produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: This requires a small amount of daylight in the final furlong that allows a hold-up horse to deliver its natural finish; Al Muqdad (Silvestre De Sousa, strong AW form, 11/15 on similar going) and Ballybunion are the most capable of executing this if the fractions allow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Increases; Stayers Win
scenarios.trigger: If a horse jumps well and tries to lead, setting a stronger-than-expected gallop that stretches the field and rewards genuine stamina over raw speed.
scenarios.body: This shape is the least likely given the absence of any declared front-runner, but if it materialises it plays into the hands of horses with proven staying power at 7f on AW; Merry (unknown style, fresh after 92 days) and Kit Gabriel (consistent AW 7f placer) hold residual claims if the race develops with more genuine fractions.

watchPoints.text: Gunfighter won course-and-distance last time out and Jack Gilligan will know exactly where to position this horse in a sprint finish — watch if he gets a trouble-free run into the straight.

Lessay's AW course-and-distance win and strong standard-going record make it the standout if it can secure a handy berth despite the redistribution; watch early in the straight to see if it gets first run.

Quick Quasar wore blinkers when winning last time and Luke Morris may attempt to ride more prominently than the map suggests — if it secures a forward position from stall draw it could bounce straight to the front.

Al Muqdad is running for the third time in 24 days and while going suitability is outstanding, watch whether Silvestre De Sousa elects to produce a late run or attempts to get closer early — the riding style will define whether this compact field gives him a gap.

With 12 runners and virtually no confirmed pace, watch the opening furlong for any horse that jumps well and attempts to steal a march — even a modest lead could be decisive in this shape if the rest of the field waits.|

races.name: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tarot
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 3yo for Roger Varian with strong Standard-going credentials and a recent win at this course and distance; hood reported and Sean Bowen claiming, 20 days fresh — well placed to exploit the pace map from second or third.
runners_data.comment: Tarot landed the spoils three starts back and arrives here on a sharp 20-day turnaround with a trainer firing at 40% in the last fortnight — strong leading arguments. The concern is back-to-back disappointing finishes since that win.

runners_data.name: Callahan
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly returning after a 153-day absence for James Owen, which is a significant fitness concern; won here over 7f on Standard going but needs more pace than this race is likely to generate to deliver her best.
runners_data.comment: Callahan won three starts back but has posted back-to-back unplaced efforts since, and 153 days off the track is a real question mark; she has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 35% keeps her interesting despite the fitness concern.

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Consistent 5yo placed at this track over 7f who wants to race prominently; the crowded early pace means she is likely to end up further back than she'd prefer, which tempers her prospects in a shape that rewards those who get their natural slot.
runners_data.comment: Bella Bisbee ran second last time out, which is a positive, but she sits ranked seventh of nine on our figures and has been largely inconsistent in recent starts — that second aside, she's hard to fancy at a lofty 129 lb, though she has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Paris Babe
runners_data.note: Top weight at 144lbs and a hold-up filly who has been running in shorter trips on Soft ground recently; the 70-day absence and steady pace are against her, though the hg:p headgear change and a return to 7f Standard may sharpen her up.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts, Paris Babe nonetheless boasts a rating of 96 — the highest in the field — and has run over today's distance and going before. Fresh off a 70-day break from stall nine on 144 lb, she's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who won here over 7f on Standard going last time; Charlie Johnston yard in fair 14-day form and Oliver Stammers takes the ride — the key question is whether she can back up quickly enough after 14 days to dominate from the front again.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below the top-rated runner on our figures and ranked eighth of nine, Carnival Of Light is hard to fancy despite winning last time out. She has run over today's trip and going, and 14 days between runs suggests she is fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Orchid
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 4yo for George Boughey who has form on Standard going at this trip; the 62-day break is worth noting and she has not struck on Standard ground in recent outings, but the hg:t headgear suggests connections are trying to sharpen her response.
runners_data.comment: Orchid shaped with promise when fourth three starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going — our rating of 90 suggests she's better than her official mark of 83. The worry is that she's been winless in recent starts and returns after 62 days off.

runners_data.name: Inside Story
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 3yo for James Tate, won here over 6f Standard and ran a solid fourth at 7f on Standard — Silvestre De Sousa takes over and the step up to 7f with a clear pace to follow could bring out more improvement.
runners_data.comment: Inside Story showed she can win at this level with a victory five starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — our rating of 91 marks her out as a strong threat from stall 2. The risk is a run of four consecutive below-par efforts since that win.

runners_data.name: Lili Marleen
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a clear tendency to fade in the finish flagged in her profile; trainer Jack Jones has had no winners in the last 14 days from 16 runners, and the sharp drop back from 8f to 7f with a Standard surface record of only one win makes this a difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Lili Marleen shaped with promise when winning four starts back and was third five starts back, but her last two outings have produced a fall and a pull-up — forgiveness is needed before she can be trusted again, though she remains unexposed and open to better.

runners_data.name: Ghisa
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer for Charlie Fellowes who has won on Standard over 7f but finds himself mapped back into midfield due to the congested pace positions; Daniel Muscutt rides and the hg:h hood is noted, but racing out of role in a pace-bound shape limits his upside here.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to third last time out after a run of disappointing efforts, and she has experience over today's trip and going — but that 43-day absence and a tough 127 lb to carry from stall 8 leave questions unanswered about where she is right now.

races.paceDynamic: Carnival Of Light is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a nine-runner field over Wolverhampton's 7f, she should control this race from the gates at a sustainable, uncontested tempo. Tarot, Orchid, and Inside Story are all prominent-running types who will look to sit just behind the leader, creating a compact early order rather than a pressured gallop. The moderate, even pace set by Carnival Of Light means the race is unlikely to truly test the field until the home straight, favouring those who can travel comfortably in the first two or three positions and quicken on a sound surface. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those who can sit just off the pace, as the steady tempo will give them cover without burning them out, while true hold-up types will be asked to produce their run from further back than the pace warrants. Note that the field contains more prominent-wanting types than can all secure their natural positions — Ghisa and Bella Bisbee are both true prominent racers who will instead find themselves shuffled into midfield, with Carnival Of Light, Tarot, and Orchid the likeliest to actually command the favoured positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Carnival Of Light Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Carnival Of Light secures the rail and dictates an uncontested, measured pace throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets a fair but not punishing gallop that leaves her full of running into the straight, and with no rivals willing to pressurise her the prominent-to-lead profile is rewarded as she holds on or kicks clear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Tarot or Orchid sit a length off the pace and produce a decisive challenge once Carnival Of Light's advantage is absorbed in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The steady tempo keeps prominent-sitting rivals in a perfect position to strike, with enough petrol in the tank to quicken past a front-runner who has been working harder than she looks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough in the first half to string the field out and leave something for Callahan or Paris Babe to run into.
scenarios.body: Callahan makes her seasonal return after 153 days here and Paris Babe carries the highest weight but both are true hold-up types who need more tempo than this race is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Scramble Home
scenarios.trigger: If Carnival Of Light stops sharply inside the final furlong having gone too freely from the front.
scenarios.body: A disorganised sprint finish from the home turn would see prominent-midfield horses like Ghisa or Bella Bisbee — both natural up-with-the-pace types shuffled back — catch the leaders in a flat-out dash.

watchPoints.text: Carnival Of Light — if she jumps cleanly and secures the rail uncontested, she controls the race tempo entirely; watch whether any rival attempts to pressurise her in the first two furlongs or whether she's left completely alone.

Tarot — fits the pace map ideally at OR 83 for Roger Varian and has won at this course and distance on Standard; watch whether Sean Bowen slots him into the pocket behind Carnival Of Light from the off, which would be the textbook move.

Ghisa and Bella Bisbee — both want to be prominent but cannot both hold that position; watch how they jump and whether one bursts through to claim a forward slot, as any scrimmaging for position could unsettle the early shape.

Callahan — Cieren Fallon on a hold-up type returning from 153 days; watch the betting market closely for any significant support as a confidence indicator, given the fitness question mark over a horse absent since autumn.

Inside Story — Silvestre De Sousa's booking for this James Tate 3yo on a going and trip combination where she has placed; watch for her to be ridden to track the pace rather than drop back, as a forward-tracking ride would suit this race shape perfectly.

races.name: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Won twice at Wolverhampton at 10f on Standard, showing genuine course-and-distance form, but a finish of 8th last time at Goodwood on Good adds a minor distance question stepping back up; a natural hold-up horse who should secure a clean rearward berth in this field, with Jack Gilligan booking a plus.
runners_data.comment: Lexington Express won three times in her last six starts, including back-to-back wins three and four starts back, but has drifted to eighth last time out, and at 133 lb from stall 11 she faces a stiff ask, though she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Suggy
runners_data.note: Consistent at-a-distance placer who arrives on the back of a win at 8f Standard and fits the genuine hold-up mould naturally; Charles Hills yard in T14 form (3/18) and Daniel Muscutt a solid booking — a true rear-ranker who should get exactly the run he wants.
runners_data.comment: Suggy arrives on the back of a win last time out and has won twice in his last five starts, showing he knows how to find the line; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 25 days between runs suggests he returns fresh — the main risk is that mid-sequence eighth raising questions about consistency.

runners_data.name: Always Blue
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's filly has placed at 10f on Good and comes into this with valid form claims, but she is a true hold-up horse who is likely to find herself racing closer to mid-pack than suits given the volume of similar types; her chance is tempered by that positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a best recent effort of second three starts back, Always Blue returns after 53 days off carrying 133 lb from stall 10; she has run over today's trip, but rated 70 on our figures, she looks up against it here.

runners_data.name: Highland Shah
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon's mount has a win and a third on Standard going and steps up to 1m½f from 7f starts, making the stamina test the key question; naturally prominent and should see out a place in the front group if the trip is within range.
runners_data.comment: Highland Shah ran a solid third last time out, and a winner two starts back, with going experience an asset here. Carrying 132 lb from stall two, he arrives on a sharp 22-day turnaround in good heart, and our figures suggest he holds strong claims.

runners_data.name: Lightning Glory
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — Simon & Ed Crisford's colt has an enviable Standard record and De Sousa will dictate from the front with no obvious challenger; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he is mapped as prominent but is actually the confirmed leader, and his hold on the race depends on keeping the gallop within his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without finding the winner's enclosure, Lightning Glory has finished third or better three times in her last five starts but is yet to win in recent form; she has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 76 gives her a squeak.

runners_data.name: Constant Star
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's colt has a win on Standard at 7f and a placing at 8f, and Luke Morris can exploit a natural prominent position sitting just off Lightning Glory; T14 in excellent nick (5/16) and this step to 1m½f is the only unproven element.
runners_data.comment: Constant Star won three starts back and was second four starts back, giving her a solid recent platform; she has run over today's trip and going, returns fit on 26 days' rest from stall 1 carrying 135 lb, though her last two runs — fifth and eighth — are the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Lillie Margot
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe's filly won at 8f Good and placed at 8f Standard, bringing strong recent form, but the 1m½f trip is a new test; Jack Doughty rides and her natural hold-up style means she needs the pace to have told on those ahead before she can strike.
runners_data.comment: Lillie Margot arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a third last time out, and she has run over today's distance and going before — her 78 rating topping this field of eleven makes her a clear threat, though 134 lb is the obvious burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: The Stone Power
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's colt placed at 10f Standard and 7f Standard, suggesting the 1m½f trip should suit in principle; Edward Greatrex keeps the ride and he is a natural front-foot racer, but OR=69 leaves him needing the conditions to fall his way against better-rated rivals.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, The Stone Power does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and third-place finishes two and three starts back show some consistency; the fourth last time out is less encouraging, and 130 lb from stall nine adds to his task.

runners_data.name: India Gold
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway's runner is a genuine prominent type who has been pushed back to midfield on the map simply because there are too many forward-going horses; her last two runs — 9th and 2nd — are form either side of a wide range and Tyler Heard on a 0/1 T14 count for the yard is a mild negative.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well enough when second last time out, but her ninth two starts back is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 48 days off means fitness is the query for India Gold off 128 lb from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Golden Mabel
runners_data.note: Lisa Williamson's filly is a confirmed hold-up operator by history but finds herself mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; a form string of 885786 tells a difficult story and OR=57 is the lowest in the field, making it hard to identify a winning scenario even in a race that plays to her style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with finishes no better than fifth in that sequence, Golden Mabel faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but little else from recent form encourages.

runners_data.name: Yes Waliim
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's charge arrives on a sprint background (all recent runs at 5-6f) stepping sharply up to 1m½f, which is the dominant concern; a genuine hold-up type displaced into mid-pack on the map, and the distance query combined with OR=57 and a 38-day absence makes this a very speculative runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Yes Waliim faces a stiff task here; he does strip fit enough at 38 days since his last run and has run over today's going before, but his recent form offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Lightning Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push them from the outset, Silvestre De Sousa should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m½f trip on Standard Wolverhampton sand. Highland Glory, Constant Star, and The Stone Power will press forward into prominent positions behind, creating a competitive but not chaotic pace picture that gives the leader a sustainable advantage rather than burning them up early. The field carries a significant concentration of hold-up types — Always Blue, Golden Mabel, Yes Waliim, and Lexington Express — several of whom have been redistributed in the map because there is simply more hold-up horses than the rear of the field can accommodate; of those, Lexington Express and Suggy are most likely to secure a genuine rearward berth, while Always Blue and Golden Mabel may find themselves racing closer than ideal. A race run at a fair, uncontested clip with a settled leader strongly favours prominent racers who track the pace without burning energy, as late closers will face a race that has not been run fast enough to empty the tank of those up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lightning Glory Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lightning Glory secures an uncontested lead and De Sousa dictates a steady-to-fair gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Lightning Glory dictates every fraction from the front, never over-exerting, and the race turns into a test of class and fitness rather than stamina slog; prominent horses who track efficiently are gifted the slipstream into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and prominent runners tracking Lightning Glory unleash a strong finish in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Constant Star or Highland Shah, sitting a length or two off the lead with cover, inherit the race as Lightning Glory's advantage is neutralised by sustained gallop; this shape rewards horses whose prominent style is natural and unforced.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves surprisingly strong and the front-runners tighten each other up enough to leave a gap for a late run.
scenarios.body: Lexington Express and Suggy, genuine hold-up types who secure the rear naturally, would be best-placed to benefit if fatigue hits those upfront entering the final furlong; however this scenario is partially undermined by the number of redistributed hold-up horses who may not achieve true rearward positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types jostle for position early and the race fractures with an uneven gallop causing a muddled finish.
scenarios.body: An erratic pace that stops and starts would randomise the result, benefiting horses who are versatile enough to adapt mid-race; India Gold and Lexington Express, both natural forwardly-placed types, could capitalise if they find daylight through a compressed field.

watchPoints.text: Lightning Glory sets the pace without a challenger — if De Sousa allows the lead to lengthen unchecked entering the back straight, the race could be over before the final turn.

Yes Waliim steps from 6f sprint form to 1m½f for the first time — watch for early signs of the trip stretching credulity in the back straight, which could compromise her and tighten up those immediately behind.

India Gold and Always Blue are natural prominent and hold-up types respectively who are likely to be racing out of their preferred positions — any jostling for ground in the first three furlongs could create an untidy pace profile.
Constant Star's trainer Tom Clover holds a strong T14 strike rate (5/16) — watch whether Luke Morris rides with confidence to sit second and use that form momentum.

Lexington Express has three wins and a placing in five visits to Wolverhampton at similar trips on Standard — if Gilligan gets a clean passage from the rear, sectionals in the final furlong will be worth noting for future reference.

races.name: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Joseph
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with strong similar-going form (2W4P on Standard), returning off 25 days in first-time hood headgear — John Butler's T14 strike-rate of 3/14 is modest but the horse's own record at this trip and surface is the main asset; will need clean air coming off the bend.
runners_data.comment: Joseph arrives here on the back of a win three starts back and has run on today's going before, making him a live threat off a mark of 69. The concern is that he has been out of the frame in two of his last three runs.

runners_data.name: Jodhpur Blue
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' five-year-old has a solid placing record (0W4P on similar going) but his true closer's style means he'll likely find himself racing closer to the pace than he'd prefer in this field of hold-up types, which may blunt his finishing kick in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Jodhpur Blue is a consistent performer whose recent form reads four runner-up finishes and a third in his last six starts, and he has experience of today's distance and going — the main concern is turning persistent placing into something more, as he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Roc De Fer
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old is fresh off a 4-day turnaround after winning over 11f on Standard, giving him strong course-and-going claims — a natural hold-up horse who will be pushed forward into midfield by the race shape, which could suit if he settles and conserves energy through the bends.
runners_data.comment: Roc De Fer comes here on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, with a trainer firing at 41% in the last fortnight. The quick four-day turnaround is the only query, but the form trends his way.

runners_data.name: Louie's Folly
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's four-year-old has no wins from 13 runs on similar going and his best form has come at significantly longer distances (16-22f), so this 1m4f trip may simply be too short; the 3lb claimer Laura Coughlan rides but the historical form is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Louie's Folly heads here ranked sixth of seven on our figures, and an eighth last time out does little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 23 days between runs suggests she's fresh.

runners_data.name: Dartmouth Jet
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner ridden by Silvestre De Sousa, returning from 71 days off for John Mackie — his two wins have both come at 16f on Good at Goodwood, so this shorter Standard Polytrack trip is a slight unknown, but his positional advantage as sole pace-setter is the defining tactical factor in this race.
runners_data.comment: Rated 20 lb above his official mark, Dartmouth Jet brings solid claims off what looks a lenient weight, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main concern is a return from 71 days off, winless in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Much
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old has shown only modest form over 10f on soft and good ground and steps up markedly in trip here — Daniel Muscutt rides but the lack of distance form and absence of similar-going runs (no Standard surface history) creates genuine uncertainty about whether this trip will unlock improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Much faces a stiff task here; 52 days off adds a fitness query, though he has a weight of 130 lb to carry and little recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old has won twice on soft ground and placed on Standard (3 runs, 0W on Standard) — a natural hold-up horse who will race further forward than ideal in this congested field, and the 4-day turnaround following his last run is a minor flag, though his prior headgear flag and progressive profile keep him relevant.
runners_data.comment: Fans Favourite has won twice in his last five starts, with back-to-back victories two and three starts back, though he faded to fifth last time out on a quick four-day turnaround; he has experience of today's trip and going, but 130 lb is a stiff burden.

races.paceDynamic: Dartmouth Jet is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field over 1m4f on Wolverhampton's standard Polytrack surface, and with no other confirmed pace-setter to challenge him, he is near-certain to dictate at whatever tempo Silvestre De Sousa chooses from the front. The absence of serious early pressure means the pace is likely to be controlled and sustainable — a classic lone-leader scenario where Dartmouth Jet can set a measured gallop and make the others work for their position rather than being dragged into a test. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types who will be forced to make ground from the middle to rear, and the key question is whether any of them can generate sufficient late momentum on what will likely be a steady-to-moderate pace. This race shape firmly favours a prominent racer or a hold-up horse with a powerful sustained finish rather than a pure late sprinter — in a one-paced gallop at Wolverhampton's turning track, those who can travel smoothly in midfield and pick up from the two-pole are best placed. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Jodhpur Blue, Fans Favourite, Roc De Fer, Louie's Folly, and Joseph are all true hold-up horses, and several will be forced to race closer to the pace than is natural for them; Dartmouth Jet and Joseph (in terms of prior form pattern) are most likely to secure a cleaner positional run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dartmouth Jet Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Dartmouth Jet is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the outset and sets a pace that does not invite a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: Silvestre De Sousa controls the fractions on the front-running Dartmouth Jet, and the field's hold-up types are left with too much ground to make up around Wolverhampton's tight bends entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel In Lone Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Dartmouth Jet sets a pace fractionally too brisk for the distance, leaving him vulnerable in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse with a strong, sustained finish — ideally one who has travelled smoothly in midfield — picks up the leader inside the final quarter-mile as Dartmouth Jet's effort fades on the turn for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly modest and the hold-up pack converge together, creating a sprint finish from off the pace.
scenarios.body: With several horses compressed into midfield through no choice of their own, the one with the best turn of foot and clearest run wins a messy late scramble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Steady Race
scenarios.trigger: If early positioning causes interference on Wolverhampton's tight early bends, unsettling the closely-grouped hold-up pack.
scenarios.body: The bunching of five hold-up types creates traffic problems and checked momentum in the back straight, leaving the cleanest-travelling horse to benefit regardless of style.

watchPoints.text: Dartmouth Jet will shape this entire race — watch whether Silvestre De Sousa allows him to stride on or deliberately sits on the front end, as even a small pace variation will determine whether the closers can get back.

The five genuine hold-up horses (Joseph, Jodhpur Blue, Roc De Fer, Fans Favourite, Louie's Folly) will compete for the same midfield-to-rear positions on the first bend — watch for crowding and checked runs as they sort themselves out early on Wolverhampton's tight opening turn.

Roc De Fer runs for the second time in four days; watch whether Luke Morris rides him conservatively to preserve energy, as a hard race midweek could blunt what looked like a sharp performance last time.

Much has no recorded runs on Standard going and has only raced at 10f — watch whether Daniel Muscutt rides him prominently to compensate for the unknown trip, which would change the positional map materially.
Joseph wears headgear for the first time today — watch his early behaviour and whether the hood settles him into his usual patient hold-up style or prompts him to race more keenly than intended.

races.name: Cavani Fashion Forward Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Moving Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with a genuine 2nd on Standard AW at 6f in recent form, but trainer Loughnane has 0 wins from 7 runners over 14 days and the 0/9 form figure is a concern; this race shape suits the style but consistency is the question.
runners_data.comment: Moving Force showed plenty when finishing a second three starts back, and he returns in good nick just 17 days later with experience of today's trip and ground — though he's winless in recent starts and will need to bounce back sharply from two below-par efforts since.

runners_data.name: American Style
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner confirmed as the lone front-runner here, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution — he ran 3rd on STA at 6f recently but faces a competitive field; his unchallenged lead is the key tactical asset if rivals allow it.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and placed five starts back too, American Style arrives on the back of a 17-day break with experience over today's trip and going. He carries 138 lb from stall 8, though a trainer in cold form is the one reservation against him.

runners_data.name: Blinky
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been at 5f and he steps up to 6f today, which is an unproven trip — headgear (p) noted, and while he has won on Standard going, the extra furlong on AW at Wolverhampton is an untested variable that should temper confidence.
runners_data.comment: Blinky has run over today's trip and going before, and his back-to-back fourths in his last two starts suggest a horse knocking on the door — our rating of 86 makes him a genuine threat at stall 4. The risk is he's yet to convert that consistency into a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Papa Cocktail
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran who is relentlessly consistent at 6f on Good, with six placed efforts in his last five, but his sim-going record on Standard is just 1W from 10 attempts — prominent style suits this race shape but the AW surface record is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Papa Cocktail has been consistently placed in recent starts — third last time out and a second two starts back — and has experience of today's distance and going; the main risk is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Maris Angel
runners_data.note: Impressive five-win record including three consecutive wins on Standard AW at 6f, but has been pushed back to midfield on the map because the prominent berths are taken — her natural style is forward-going, and if she can't assert early, the STYLE_FIT discount applies; 59 days off is also a flag.
runners_data.comment: A 59-day absence and a ranking of ninth of ten on our figures make her hard to fancy despite solid recent form — third two starts back and a winner three starts back (and the two before that). Has run over today's trip and going, and 134 lb is the weight she carries from stall 7.

runners_data.name: HK Fourteen
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's runner ships back quickly (7 days) having struggled in recent runs (0W0P in last five sim-going attempts); a genuine prominent runner whose position has been absorbed by other pace in this field, reducing his chance in this configuration.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, HK Fourteen steps back up quickly after finishing eighth last time out, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; yet to find consistency, he faces an uphill task from stall six carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Anfield
runners_data.note: Tom Clover in good form (5/16 over 14 days) and this 3yo has course form with a 2nd on STA at 6f — headgear (h) noted; prominent style fits the race map but two blanks since that placed effort and a 34-day absence temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Hasn't hit the frame in his last two starts, though a winner and twice runner-up in the three runs before that show he retains ability; has run over today's trip and carries 132 lb from stall two, leaving him with something to prove on recent form.

runners_data.name: Hugh
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) and only three career runs to analyse, but the 2nd on Standard 6f is solid form for this grade — Clive Cox has 3 runners placed in 14 days and Georgia Dobie's claim could be significant if Hugh settles and produces a late finish; 52-day break is the main risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Hugh is hard to fancy here; 52 days off adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and going before, and that second two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Three wins on Standard AW at 6f, including a recent course success, give him the strongest course-and-distance profile in the race — hold-up style is ideally suited to the expected pace shape, and Cieren Fallon is a strong booking; the 14-day turnaround on a 3yo is manageable.
runners_data.comment: King Of Chaos has shown he can win — twice in his last six starts, including last time out — but ranked eighth of ten on our figures with a speed rating of 68, the bare form makes him hard to fancy despite the recent winning run and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Angel Love
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Standard and placed on STA going twice, making her course-and-going profile respectable; Kevin Philippart De Foy has 2 wins from 9 over 14 days and Daniel Muscutt is an able pilot, but a 51-day absence and two blanks since her win require monitoring.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back and third four starts back give Angel Love a decent recent profile, but she's been below par in her last two outings and returns after a 51-day absence; experience over today's trip and going offers some reassurance.

races.paceDynamic: American Style is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on a flat Wolverhampton AW 6f, is likely to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being seriously pressured for the lead. Papa Cocktail and Angel Of Anfield are genuine prominent types who should sit just off the pace in second and third, giving this race a sensibly-strung-out shape rather than a chaotic scramble. The field holds more prominent-profile horses than the race can accommodate — Maris Angel and HK Fourteen are natural front-to-prominent runners but have been redistributed to midfield on the map, as American Style and Papa Cocktail are overwhelmingly more likely to physically occupy those forward berths. A single, uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on a flat track strongly favours hold-up horses with a clean turn of foot — King Of Chaos and Moving Force, closing from off the pace, are the profiles this shape sets up best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If American Style controls from the front unchallenged and the pace remains honest but not brutal, setting up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: American Style bowls along at a steady clip with Papa Cocktail and Angel Of Anfield tracking, but the moderate tempo means the back-straight pace is insufficient to soften up the leaders — the closers get a clean run and arrive in numbers. King Of Chaos, with three wins on Standard AW at 6f and a proven turn of foot, and Moving Force, whose 2nd on similar going shows latent ability, are perfectly positioned to sweep through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely even and the prominent runners travel supremely well throughout, allowing the mid-race leaders to hold on.
scenarios.body: Papa Cocktail's consistent handicap form (six placed efforts in last five at 6f on Good) allows him to stalk the pace and pounce before the closers wind up, and Angel Of Anfield, with course form (2nd on STA at 6f), can do likewise if holding his 3yo ability. Angel Love's prior wins on Standard 6f also make her a candidate if she translates her close-up style into a well-timed challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Left Flat
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or is unusually slow, with no horse able to reel in a front-runner who dictates at their own speed.
scenarios.body: American Style, given full control and a very slow early pace, could steal enough margin to hold on against tiring rivals; his STYLE_FIT flag is a concern but if unchallenged the race is his to lose. Papa Cocktail's relentless prominent style would also benefit if the pace is falsely slow, as he can track and pounce before the hold-up horses find stride.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Pair Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Maris Angel or HK Fourteen force their way to the front despite the redistribution, creating a faster-than-expected pace that scrambles the race shape.
scenarios.body: A messy pace with multiple horses vying for position would suit a horse with a proven ability to relax off the pace and still finish powerfully, such as King Of Chaos (three STA wins at 6f) or Hugh if he translates his 2nd-on-STA form into this quicker gallop. However, this shape has lower probability precisely because these horses are unlikely to secure their natural positions against established pace-setters.

watchPoints.text: King Of Chaos has three wins on Standard AW 6f and Cieren Fallon's positioning from a hold-up role could prove decisive if American Style sets a single uncontested gallop — watch him accelerate from the two-furlong pole.

Maris Angel and HK Fourteen are natural prominent runners who cannot both get their preferred position; if either forces their way forward at the start, the pace dynamic changes materially and the scenario probabilities shift.
Blinky runs over 6f for the first time in all five recent starts at 5f — if he gets outpaced early on the longer trip, his chance evaporates quickly on this flat AW circuit.

Papa Cocktail's Standard AW sim-going record is 1 win from 10 attempts despite being highly consistent on Good ground — punters relying on his form string alone may be underestimating the surface switch.

Angel Of Anfield's trainer Tom Clover is in a productive 14-day spell (5/16); if the 34-day break has freshened this 3yo and the headgear holds him together, he could outrun a big price tracking the pace from second.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old in form (won 14 days ago over C&D) and trainer Perratt is in a purple patch at 4/13 over 14 days; naturally a hold-up horse but the redistribution tag reflects how unlikely he is to find genuine space at the rear in a field of pure closers, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Sixcor won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but he heads into this carrying 139 lb just four days on, ranks last of six on our figures, and his official mark of 44 reflects a modest profile that makes him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Bust A Moon
runners_data.note: 60-day absence is a concern at this level, and the sim-going record of 0W0P from 15 runs on Standard is a significant red flag; naturally races from the rear but with several rivals doing the same, finding clean air late may prove impossible.
runners_data.comment: Bust A Moon showed promise with a third five starts back, and he has course conditions experience with previous runs over this distance and going; winless in recent starts, but our rating of 58 marks him as the one to beat from stall 5 off 135 lb after a 60-day break.

runners_data.name: Captain Kinsella
runners_data.note: Trainer Gallagher is 0/9 over the 14-day window, which is a cold stat; has a modest 0W0P record from 11 Standard-going runs, and though the headgear (tp) offers some hope, the redistribution means he cannot settle into his natural role here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Captain Kinsella nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and at 135 lb from stall four he remains a leading danger here — though his tendency to finish mid-pack or worse is the concern to overcome.

runners_data.name: Fancy Dancer
runners_data.note: Best of the non-redistributed hold-up types, with Burton striking at 1/2 in the trainer 14-day window and the only runner in the field with a winning record on similar going (1W2P from 7 sim-going runs); 24 days since last run is not a concern at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Fancy Dancer nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table and has been freshened up nicely over 24 days; our rating of 58 marks her out as a genuine threat, though she'll need to find more at the finish than recent efforts suggest.

runners_data.name: Happier
runners_data.note: Jockey Jack Doughty takes the ride for Keighley, who is 0/4 over 14 days; recent form includes a 4th at 6f on Good suggesting some ability, though the sim-going record of 0W1P from only 3 runs is thin and the step back to 5f needs proving.
runners_data.comment: Happier brings distance-and-going experience to this and is freshly turned out just 10 days after her last start, with a fourth three starts back hinting at better lurking; drawn in stall one, she carries 135 lb, and the risk is that she has been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Poetic Jack
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell is 0/11 over 14 days, which is a very cold yard angle; has decent place form on AW Standard (2P from 11 runs) and the 52-day absence is a note of caution, but as a redistributed hold-up type he is unlikely to find the back of the field he needs in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a pair of fourths further back his best recent efforts, Poetic Jack has little to recommend him on form, though he has run over today's distance and going before and our figures suggest he rates a shade above his official mark.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this six-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no natural front-runner to set the race alight — the early stages at Wolverhampton's 5f are likely to be tentative and tactically awkward, with runners shuffling for position rather than blazing clear. Whoever edges forward from the gates will find themselves leading by default rather than by design, and the race will almost certainly compress into a wall-to-wall sprint in the final two furlongs. The absence of any genuine pace means the sectionals will be slow early and fast late, suiting horses who can finish strongly from just off a crawl — though in a race this short, "hold-up" is largely a misnomer and position off a slow gallop becomes the key variable. Fancy Dancer and Happier, as the two runners not tagged [REDISTRIBUTED], are best placed to adapt; the field also contains Sixcor, Bust A Moon, Captain Kinsella, and Poetic Jack as true hold-up types who cannot all find the rear positions they prefer, meaning several will race out of role and their chances are correspondingly undermined. The race shape firmly favours horses with genuine finishing speed who can travel close enough to the eventual pace to pounce in the last 100 yards — a sprint-finish profile benefits Fancy Dancer and Happier most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Crawl Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no runner commits early and the field drifts into a dawdle before a furious final-furlong dash.
scenarios.body: A near-identical pace is set by whoever blinks first, compressing the field and turning the race into a 1f dash; horses positioned just behind the leader are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Drift Forward Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one runner, likely Fancy Dancer or Happier, decides to push on from halfway to try to exploit the pace vacuum.
scenarios.body: The race fragments slightly as one horse kicks clear at the 2f pole with no genuine challenger willing to match strides early; the front-runner benefits from the resulting momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners simultaneously decide to push up, creating a brief surge of pace before a chaotic final furlong.
scenarios.body: The compressed sprint becomes a rough, wide-open scramble with no horse able to settle into a rhythm; exposed horses with strong finishing speed and course form hold an edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to string the field out and allow late finishers to close.
scenarios.body: Given the wholesale redistribution of true hold-up runners across the field, this depends on horses racing in their natural role — a scenario weakened considerably by the number tagged [REDISTRIBUTED].

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Fancy Dancer's jockey Luke Morris instinctively pushes forward from the gate — if he does, Fancy Dancer could land a soft lead by default and dictate this entire sprint.

Sixcor's recent win over C&D 14 days ago gives him fitness and course knowledge, but his hold-up style in a race with no genuine pace is a contradiction that could cost him a clear run in the closing stages.
Bust A Moon's 60-day absence combined with a 0W0P record on Standard going makes him a significant each-way risk regardless of the race shape — monitor market confidence carefully before the off.

Captain Kinsella's tongue strap (tp headgear) is worth noting as it suggests a breathing or settling issue — in a race that may start slowly and then explode, any horse with a breathing concern faces an awkward tactical test.

With all six runners sharing the same hold-up profile, draw position could become decisive at Wolverhampton's 5f — horses drawn towards the inside rail may find themselves boxed in during the inevitable late sprint.
